acceptance: make pr-rerun on a run whose only failure is a would-block duration verdict re-runs the fast-tier shards, so the verdict is computed from newly measured timings.
A regression test shows a failed-jobs-only rerun is not selected for that case, and that other failure kinds keep failed-jobs-only reruns.
pr-arm's would-block refusal names the rerun remedy alongside the baseline remedy.
description:
Problem. The fast-tier duration gate in the core job can report would-block from slow-runner noise alone (tracked in ci-fast-duration-gate-slow-runner-margin-20261101). The remedy is fresh timings, but make pr-rerun (scripts/pr_rerun.py rerun_arguments) re-runs only failed jobs of a failed run. The fast-tier shards passed, so only the core aggregate re-runs, and it re-reads the saved fast-junit artifact and reproduces the identical verdict. Observed on #4002 (a PR that only deletes tests): summed ratio 1.313, delta +442.6 s, median per-test ratio 1.010 on attempt 1, and exactly 1.313 again on the failed-jobs rerun (attempt 2). A full `gh run rerun` of the same run (attempt 3) measured 1.155 and passed. pr-arm's refusal text offers only 'remove the slowdown, or regenerate the baseline', neither of which applies to runner noise.

Change. When the only failure is a would-block duration verdict, make pr-rerun re-run the whole CI run (or the fast-tier shards plus core) so new timings are measured, and pr-arm's refusal names that remedy. A real slowdown must still block after the fresh measurement.
